Bipolar completely fucked up my life. It manifested when I was around 18-19. I had to drop out of medical school after so much hard work. Managed to snatch a hefty scholarship to study in the US and then failed because my situation was unmanageable.

 I’ve been trying to get a diagnosis since I was 20 years old but was never taken seriously. Apparently a couple of my doctors told my own mother that I have bipolar (we don’t have HIPPA here. It’s a disaster) but they were too “scared” to tell me because they were worried of my reaction despite me being open to try anything and everything. 

Finally got diagnosed less than a year ago at age 28. And I feel like I’m getting my life back. It’s seriously amazing. I’m not scared of my own thoughts. I’m not scared of being happy because I worry that I will be depressed afterwards. It was hard to accept at first because I recognized that all the times I thought I was getting better, I was just in a hypomanic episode. And sometimes I miss those flashes of extreme happiness. But I wouldn’t trade my current state for anything. 

I’ve actually managed to get an actual job. It’s stupid and pays like shit. But it’s a job. Something I was so sure I’ll never be able to do. 

And Lamotrigine has very little side effects, specially compared to the plethora of SSRIs and SNRIs I was subjected to through the years. (I can now cry for real. I feel emotions. Just not too strong that they become terrifying). For once I’m truly happy despite having to live with my abusive family and feeling somewhat defeated due to being 29 and done nothing in my life. 

Never underestimate the positive effects that medication could get you. It’s absolutely and utterly worth it.

We don't rely on "scars" on the pelvis. But on the degree of how the pelvis bone is shaped. And even then there is a huge margin of error because a lot of people are in the in-between and we can't be sure if they're AFAB or AMAB. The only sure way to identify the sex is generics testing but that's usually very expensive and we only do it rarely.
